0: Back in 2023 I wrote an article called “Downloading large models was agony”,
1: Back then Hugging Face needed a VPN to be usable here, and models were a dozen gigabytes or more, so bandwidth was tight. There were mirror sites, but they were neither complete nor stable.
2: Today, if you ask where to download an open model first in China, the answer is unquestionably ModelScope. Downloads are fast, and essentially every open model, at home or abroad, is listed the moment it appears — it has become the country's largest open-model community (and not only for models).
4: The model hub is ModelScope's basic building block. The platform groups models by task type (text generation, image classification, speech recognition and so on) and supports keyword search with multi-dimensional filtering.
5: If you already know the model's name, just search for it.
6: If you have not settled on one yet, first be clear about what you want the model to do.
7: For example, to turn recordings into text, start from speech recognition, then narrow things down by language, parameter scale, runtime framework and licence.
8: To find the model that genuinely fits your business, read the chapter “Turning a business problem into a model task”.
10: Once you find a model that interests you, click through to its model card. Take Qwen3-ASR-1.7B as an example: the model page puts the introduction, the usage notes and the evaluation results side by side.
11: Start with what the model is and what it can do. The name, the overview and the architecture notes tell you whether you are looking in the right direction.
12: Then look at the scope: which languages it supports, what input suits it and what limits apply — all of which relate to your own task.
13: Next, the usage notes: which runtime it needs, which tools it depends on and how the input should be prepared are usually all in the examples. Reading them before you download saves you from finishing the download only to discover the environment cannot be deployed.
14: Finally, the evaluation results: which data the model was tested on and which metrics were compared, which is useful when choosing. How it really performs still takes a trial with your own data — a leaderboard is only a reference.
15: The model page also lists the files, the versions and the licence information. As the previous chapter mentioned, being able to use a model is not the same as being allowed to use it commercially,
16: When you are preparing for commercial use or for further fine-tuning, never skip this step.
17: Some models also offer an online demo; when a model can be tried directly, it helps you judge whether it is worth downloading.
19: ModelScope offers the web page, the command line, Git and the Python SDK. Below we keep using the smaller Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B so the first run is easy.
21: Open the model's file page, find the file you need and click the download button. The web route suits browsing files and downloading a small amount of content.

34: Model files are usually large, so install Git and Git LFS before downloading with Git. Once Git LFS is installed, run the initialisation and clone commands below.

36: You need not try all four routes: use the web page for a few files, the command line for terminal work, the SDK for Python projects and Git if that is already your habit.
37: Once the model is downloaded, open its usage example, point the model path at your local directory and get one input-and-output run working.
